question_text: Sequence 1: Find the next: A, C, E, G, ___

hint_ladder.title: Look at the gaps
hint_ladder.text: Notice how each letter jumps to the next. Is it moving one step at a time, or skipping some letters along the way?

hint_ladder.title: The skip rule
hint_ladder.text: From A to C, you skip B. From C to E, you skip D. From E to G, you skip F. So every time, you're moving two letters forward in the alphabet. That's your pattern.

hint_ladder.title: Apply the pattern
hint_ladder.text: Start at G. If you move two letters forward, you go to H (that's one), then to I (that's two). So the next letter in the sequence is I.

hint_ladder.title: You've got it
hint_ladder.text: The pattern is consistent: add 2 each time. G plus 2 gives you I. That's option B.

A.text: H is the very next letter after G, so it's a natural guess if you think the sequence just goes one by one. But look again: A to C skipped B, C to E skipped D, so the pattern actually skips one letter each time. H would only be correct if the pattern were +1, not +2.

B.text: Correct. The pattern adds 2 each time: A (1) to C (3), C to E (5), E to G (7), and G (7) to I (9). You're skipping one letter consistently, so I is the next logical term.

C.text: J is three letters after G (G to H is 1, H to I is 2, I to J is 3). That would mean the pattern changed to +3, but the sequence has been steadily adding 2 the whole time. Stick with the consistent skip.

D.text: K is four letters after G. That's a +4 jump, which is much bigger than the +2 pattern we've seen. It's easy to miscount when you're rushing, but always double-check the gap between the first few terms to find the real rhythm.

next_time_rule: For letter sequences, find the skip interval by comparing the first two terms. Count the letters you pass over: A to C skips B, so the interval is +2. Then just keep adding that same number. A quick trick: assign numbers to letters (A=1, B=2, etc.) and treat it like a number pattern.
deconstruct_text: Let's walk through this together. The sequence is A, C, E, G. The first thing to notice is that these aren't consecutive letters. A to C jumps over B, C to E jumps over D, and E to G jumps over F. So every step moves two letters forward in the alphabet. That's a consistent +2 pattern. Now, starting from G (the 7th letter), add 2: that brings you to the 9th letter, which is I. So the next term is I. A quick mental trick for these problems: assign each letter a number (A=1, B=2, C=3, and so on). Then the sequence becomes 1, 3, 5, 7. It's just odd numbers! The next odd number after 7 is 9, which is I. This number trick works for any letter sequence and makes spotting the pattern much faster under time pressure.
